topPRs.body:
## 🎯 Overview

This PR introduces a complete refactoring of the wallet analysis system, transforming it from a synchronous client-side implementation to an asynchronous server-side architecture with real-time updates and intelligent pagination.

## ✨ Key Features

### 1. **Asynchronous Analysis Architecture**
- Replaced synchronous client-side analysis with asynchronous server-side processing
- Analysis jobs run in the background on the server, allowing users to leave and return without losing progress
- Automatic job resumption when reopening the analyzer page
- Zombie job detection and automatic restart for stuck analysis processes

### 2. **Real-Time Progress Tracking**
- Live polling mechanism (every 5 seconds) to track analysis progress
- Persistent toast notifications showing:
  - Number of tokens discovered in real-time
  - Number of transactions analyzed
  - Completion status with automatic dismissal
- Heartbeat monitoring to detect and recover from stuck analysis jobs (2-minute timeout)

### 3. **Intelligent Token Loading**
- Auto-fetch mechanism that detects when new tokens are discovered during analysis
- Automatic token loading when analysis completes, even if the page hasn't refreshed
- Smart state management to prevent duplicate fetches and race conditions

### 4. **Infinite Scroll Pagination**
- Intersection Observer-based infinite scroll for token list
- 10 tokens loaded per page with automatic deduplication
- Dynamic "Load More" indicator with safety timeout
- Proper state reset when switching between wallets

### 5. **Enhanced UI Components**

#### CountUp Animation Component
- Smooth number animations for all metrics
- Configurable decimal places, separators, prefixes, and suffixes
- Used across all stat displays for a polished user experience

#### Optimized Result Display
- Summary data separated from paginated token results
- Top 3 "pain points" (biggest missed opportunities) calculated from full dataset
- Real-time updating of total counts during analysis
- "Updating in real-time..." indicator during active analysis

### 6. **Improved Error Handling**
- Comprehensive error states with user-friendly messages
- Automatic retry logic for failed requests
- Graceful degradation when API is unavailable
- Clear feedback for zombie job detection and recovery

### 7. **State Management Improvements**
- Complete state reset when switching wallets
- Proper cleanup of polling intervals and toast notifications
- Prevention of memory leaks with ref-based tracking
- Elimination of circular dependencies in React hooks

## 🔧 Technical Changes

### New Files
- `src/hooks/use-wallet-analysis.ts` - Core async analysis hook with polling
- `src/components/analyzer/token-analysis-list.tsx` - New token list component
- `src/components/ui/count-up.tsx` - Animated number component
- `src/services/analysis-client.service.ts` - API client for analysis endpoints

### Removed Files
- `src/hooks/use-trades-analysis.ts` - Old synchronous analysis hook
- `src/services/trades.service.ts` - Old trades service

### Modified Components
- `src/app/analyzer/client.tsx` - Refactored to use new async hook
- All analyzer components updated to use CountUp for animations
- Improved responsive design and formatting across all components

## 📊 Performance Improvements

- **Reduced initial load time**: Only fetches summary on mount, loads tokens progressively
- **Lower memory usage**: Pagination prevents loading all tokens at once
- **Better UX**: Users can navigate away and return without losing progress
- **Optimized polling**: Status polling separated from token fetching

## 🐛 Bug Fixes

- Fixed pagination not loading tokens when analysis completes
- Fixed intersection observer stale closure issues
- Fixed state not resetting when switching wallets
- Fixed circular dependency errors in React hooks
- Fixed duplicate token loading during pagination

## 🎨 UI/UX Enhancements

- Animated numbers for all statistics
- Persistent loading toast with live progress updates
- Clear visual feedback for all states (loading, processing, completed, error)
- Responsive design improvements across all breakpoints
- Better mobile layout with truncated text and flex-shrink utilities

## 🔄 Migration Notes

The new system is fully backward compatible with existing wallet addresses. Previously analyzed wallets will automatically trigger a new analysis on first visit.

## 📝 Summary

This PR represents a major architectural improvement to the wallet analyzer, moving from a synchronous client-side approach to a robust asynchronous server-side system with real-time updates, intelligent pagination, and a significantly improved user experience.

topPRs.title: feat: storage provider abstraction
topPRs.author: standujar
topPRs.body:
## What's changed

Added a storage abstraction layer to decouple from AWS, enabling local development without AWS dependencies.

## Key features

- **Local development**: Works with filesystem storage (`.local-storage/`)
- **AWS production**: Seamless AWS Secrets Manager & SSM integration
- **Auto-detection**: Automatically chooses provider based on `STORAGE_PROVIDER` env var
- **Same API**: No business logic changes needed

## Architecture

```
Application → Interfaces (ISecretStore, IParameterStore) → Adapters (AWS/Local) → Storage
```

## Setup

```bash
cp .env.example .env.local
# Add: STORAGE_PROVIDER=local
bun dev
```

## Files added

- `src/interfaces/storage/` - Abstract interfaces
- `src/adapters/storage/` - AWS & Local implementations
- `src/factories/StorageFactory.ts` - Provider factory

## Files migrated

All `src/actions/*` files now use `StorageFactory` instead of direct AWS services.

## Other changes

- Changed default port from 3000 to 3100
- Added `.local-storage/` to `.gitignore`
- Updated README with setup instructions

topContributors.summary: standujar: Drove significant architectural improvements across both the frontend and the analyser plugin this month, merging seven pull requests. Key contributions include introducing a major storage provider abstraction in `Sendo-labs/frontend#26` (+14230/-590 lines) and implementing an async wallet analysis with caching in `Sendo-labs/plugin-sendo-analyser#11`. They also implemented a queue manager for concurrent job processing (`#17`) and executed a large-scale refactor of API usage in the frontend (`#27`), removing over 16k lines of code. Their work was primarily focused on refactoring and new feature development.

Neysixx: Focused on improving the `Sendo-labs/frontend` repository this month through both refactoring and bug fixes. They merged three pull requests, most notably refactoring the color variable management system in PR #25. In addition to shipping fixes for the number font and guidelines (#20, #24), Neysixx also actively reviewed 6 pull requests from teammates. Their contributions were primarily centered on bug fixes and refactoring within the codebase.

xdrkush: Focused entirely on bug fixes this month, merging four pull requests across the `Sendo-labs/frontend` and `Sendo-labs/plugin-sendo-analyser` repositories. Their work addressed dependency management in the analyzer plugin via PRs #9 and #10, and also resolved UI formatting and wallet analyzer issues in the frontend (PR #19, #21). This activity shows a focus on maintaining stability through targeted fixes in both code and configuration files.

0xCanet: This month, 0xCanet's efforts were concentrated on a significant contribution to the `Sendo-labs/frontend` repository. They merged a single, large-scale pull request (Sendo-labs/frontend#23) titled "Fix: 0x canet," which introduced a substantial number of changes (+15682/-884 lines). This work primarily involved bug fixes, with additional focus on feature implementation and refactoring across 135 files.

Johnleouf21: Focused on deployment and initialization tasks this month, opening a pull request in Sendo-labs/leaderboard-rewards (#2) to fix program deployment on devnet. This work, which remains open, involved 3 commits and modifications across 8 files (+424/-421 lines). Their activity also included making a single comment on a pull request.
